response.answer: A prescriptive decision flowchart can use numeric cutoffs for L̂, n_cal, B, ESS, and dataset size to choose between OOB, independent calibration, or hybrid partial-holdout methods. Larger datasets and higher ESS favor independent calibration. Smaller datasets and lower ESS may benefit from OOB or hybrid methods.

results.title: Holdout vs Validation Set: How to Choose for Machine Learning
results.content: To do this, you need to split your data into different subsets: a training set, a test set, and optionally, a validation set. The holdout method is a simple way to split your data into two subsets: a training set and a test set. You use the training set to fit your model and tune its parameters, and then you use the test set to measure its performance on new data. Also, variations of test data should also be generated to validate the sensitivity of the AI models. The holdout method is a simple way to split your data into two sets: a training set and a test set. The validation set should be representative of the data and independent of the training set, but not as large as the test set. The validation method involves setting aside a portion of your data for fine-tuning your model's hyperparameters and choosing the best model before testing it on a separate test set. It helps ensure your model is well-adjusted and effective before assessing its performance on unseen data, striking a balance between training and evaluatio.K-Fold Cross-Validation is one of strategy for validation which involves dividing your dataset into "k" equally sized subsets or folds. The holdout method is a simple approach to split the data for evaluating AI models, but it can be problematic for small or imbalanced datasets. When deciding between the holdout and validation methods, consider the size and nature of your data, the complexity and variability of your model, and the resources and time available for your project. Using cross validation during training / hyperparameter optimization, while retaining a holdout set for your final evaluation is the gold standard if you have enough data and computational resources. However, it's essential to consider various factors related to the data, model, and resource constraints when choosing between the holdout and validation methods. The choice between a holdout and a validation set is one such decision, and understanding the landscape of your data, model, and computational resources will guide you in selecting the path that leads to optimal model performance and generalization.

results.title: What is Holdout Dataset | Iguazio
results.content: Data is at the heart of machine learning (ML,) because data is used to train ML models and test their performance. Using the test data to evaluate machine learning models comprehensively and reliably before they go to production is fundamental to ensuring that they provide value to the user by performing as intended, i.e., without unexpected behaviors. When labels are present (i.e., in supervised learning,) the most simple and commonly used approach for model evaluation is a *holdout dataset.* This is a specific type of test dataset which is unseen during training and used solely to gather the final model evaluation before production. This article defines what the holdout set is, discusses desirable characteristics thereof, walks through what evaluation it can provide, and finally discusses when to use the holdout dataset. The test set and holdout set are used for model evaluation. Keeping the test datasets separate from the training phase is fundamental in order to ensure that evaluation metrics reliably represent performance on new data when in production. Specifically, the test set is used to evaluate the model’s performance during experimentation and when comparing across multiple models. In practice, the test set and holdout set often coincide, mainly due to the availability of data. A good holdout dataset should be curated to ensure that it provides a reliable representation of the variety of data that the model will see in production, and generates a fair evaluation of the trained model. To evaluate the quality of a holdout set, data analysis can be performed in order to check for the following desirable characteristics:. The dataset split ratio between training, validation, and test sets depends on the total size of the available data and the chosen algorithm. The evaluation performed on the holdout set is the same as the evaluation performed on any test set. Technical and business metrics should be computed on the complete holdout set, as well as on relevant data slices, to provide a comprehensive understanding of the model’s performance. The holdout method is a special implementation of cross-validation; in fact, its complete name is “holdout cross-validation.” While the holdout method creates one train-test split, general cross-validation creates multiple train-test splits to train and evaluate the model.
